readiness.hed: Fredericksburg turns rainy this afternoon with a 60 percent chance near 66, stays unsettled into tonight, then clears out for a foggy-start, mild Monday near 71 before a sharp cooldown brings sunny but much colder air by Tuesday
readiness.insight: The National Weather Service shows no active watches or warnings for Fredericksburg this morning. Today turns rainy after noon with a 60 percent chance of light rain and a high near 66, continuing into tonight with a 50 percent chance and a low near 49. Monday starts with patchy fog before 8 a.m. then clears to mostly sunny with a high near 71, falling to the mid-60s by afternoon, before temperatures drop to a low around 36 Monday night with gusty north winds. Tuesday turns sharply colder and sunny with a high near 54 and an overnight low around 28.
actions: This afternoon's rain is the last of the mild, unsettled stretch — get any outdoor errands or church-grounds work done before noon if you want to stay dry.
Monday's patchy morning fog means an earlier commute should slow down and use headlights; it burns off by midday into the week's warmest, clearest afternoon near 71.
Monday night's wind gusts to 21 mph and a 35-degree drop in high temps by Tuesday are worth a last gutter-and-drain check and securing anything loose outdoors before the cold front moves through.

Tuesday's sunny 54-degree high with a 28-degree overnight low is the first real taste of hard cold this week — bring in sensitive plants and check on elderly neighbors before the Tuesday night freeze.
